messages:
kai: Quick note from the CB sync: different angle — can we reduce per-subqueue alloc overhead by pooling metadata and using a compact 'watermark' eviction instead of per-tenant fences?
maria: Interesting. Watermark = global ordered reclaim pointer? need to reason about fairness.
sam: Watermark could help memory but makes isolation weaker. A noisy tenant with many small windows could push the watermark and evict others' prefetches.
lee: Tradeoff: pooled metadata reduces GC churn but complicates reclamation semantics. We need deterministic reclaim order to keep tail SLOs predictable.
anika: Proposal sketch: use a two-layer map: hot-map (explicit subqueue structs for top-N heavy tenants) + cold-map (compact counters/watermarks for others). Promote/demote based on observed inflight tokens.
kai: Eviction policy: watermark-based soft-reclaim for cold-map (cheap to enforce) + explicit fence for hot-map tenants. That keeps per-tenant guarantees for heavy users while lowering cardinality cost.
maria: Also add retry-safety: when we cancel inflight due to hard-evict, we must emit an idempotency token and an eviction_reason so clients/retries can dedupe.
sam: Include metric "eviction_surface" showing percent of tenants in hot-map vs cold-map, and "watermark_moves" counter.
lee: For handoff/rebalance: cold-map checkpoints are small (last_seq_hint, queued_count), hot-map needs full kv_snapshot. That suggests different cost profiles.
anika: Telemetry: track per-map metrics + promotion/demotion events with latency cost. Retention: promotion traces 14d for debugging, eviction traces 7d.
kai: Implementation actionables:
- lee: prototype pooled-cold-map with simple watermark reclaim POC
- sam: draft idempotency header + eviction_reason spec for client SDKs
- anika: add promotion/demotion dashboards and alerts when watermark moves >X/min
- maria: capture this design in RFC follow-up with microbench numbers
ops-bot: CI: branch continuous-batching/metadata-pool pushed; tests queued.
maria: Love it. One caution: tuning promotion thresholds is critical; we should default to conservative values and iterate.
sam: Agreed. I'll add a tunable config snippet (promote_threshold=128 tokens, demote_idle_ms=300000).
lee: I'll try to keep cold-map lookup O(1) and ensure we don't add locks on the hot path.
anika: Filing telemetry and SDK tickets now. :spiral_note_book:
maria: Closing for now; will reconvene after POC benchmarks.
